1	# Statement debt: self-service step for the voice assistant
2	
3	Business analysis, working draft
4	Author: Selin Aydın (Card Self-Service, Freya Bank)
5	Date: 2 September 2026
6	Shared with: Kerem Yalçın, Burcu Tan, Mert Koç (for the service part)
7	
8	> Kerem, Burcu: this is my first pass after the two walkthroughs of the phone menu. Comments inline please, I'll collect them before we sit down with the Freya team. Anything marked **TBD** I could not close myself.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 0. In one paragraph
13	
14	Today the menu plays a fixed announcement and that's it. With the assistant we want a short conversation instead: which card, how much is owed and by when, and then two things the caller can get done without waiting for an agent (statement PDF by mail, a different statement week). Paying stays with the agents for now. Whatever else the caller brings up, we hand back to the main menu.
15	
16	## 1. Scope
17	
18	In:
19	- Debt reading for one card at a time, all four currencies we carry (Lira, Dollar, Euro, Sterling), with the due date. When the closed statement is fully paid, the "no debt" wording plus the running total.
20	- The two follow-ups: mailing the statement (only ever to the address we hold) and moving the statement week.
21	- Choosing the card, where needed.
22	
23	Out (first list, Kerem please extend):
24	- Paying the debt itself: handed to an agent.
25	- Disputes, "I paid but it doesn't show" (agent, see §7).
26	- Limits, cash advance, card blocking, anything about debit cards.
27	- Changing the e-mail address.
28	- Statements of earlier periods.
29	
30	Burcu thinks statement debt is one of the top three menu choices; she'll try to get a figure.
31	
32	## 2. How the caller arrives
33	
34	The phone menu has already identified and authenticated the caller before the hand-over. The assistant receives the customer number with the call and does not run any identity check of its own.
35	
36	**TBD:** the flow drawing we got from the vendor side has a box "second factor may be needed". I don't see why for a read-only step plus two low-risk actions; to confirm with Elçin.
37	
38	## 3. Picking the card
39	
40	The card list comes from `cards.list` (customer number in, eligible credit cards out). Then:
41	
42	| Situation | What the assistant does |
43	|---|---|
44	| Caller already named the card when arriving | If the name fits exactly one card, no selection question. |
45	| Several cards | Asks which one, with at most two example names taken from the caller's own cards: “Hangi kartınızın borcunu öğrenmek istersiniz? Örneğin, Yıldız Premium veya Yıldız Pratik diyebilirsiniz.” |
46	| Caller asks for "all my cards" | Not possible, the debt service takes one card at a time. Selection question again (counts as a failed attempt). |
47	| Name not on the list | Tells the caller there is no card with that name and reads the eligible ones again. |
48	| Two or more cards with the same name | Asks for the last four digits: “Yıldız isimli birden fazla kartınız var. Kartınızın son dört hanesini söyler misiniz?” (name of the card in place of "Yıldız") |
49	| Same name and same last four | Asks for the full card number: “Son dört hanesi aynı olan birden fazla kartınız var. Kart numaranızın tamamını söyler misiniz?” |
50	
51	Two easy cases outside the table: a single card is simply taken, no question. No eligible card at all: “Ekstre borcunu sorgulayabileceğiniz uygun bir kredi kartınız bulunmuyor. Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.”
52	
53	Notes:
54	- Digits can come as "dört iki beş üç", "kırk iki elli üç" etc. The assistant maps them to the four digits and moves on. No reading back of the digits, no "… kartınızla devam ediyorum" confirmation; the card name is said anyway at the start of the debt reading.
55	- Supplementary card holders: they see no eligible card of their own here. Tell them and ask for a different card. (Burcu, is that what the menu does today?)
56	- If the card name comes back empty from the service, introduce the card by its last four only.
57	
58	## 4. Reading the debt
59	
60	Service: `cards.balance` with the chosen card. It returns one block per currency (`debtTL`, `debtUSD`, `debtEUR`, `debtGBP`) with `statementDebt`, `minPayment`, `remainingDebt`, `remainingMinPayment`, `totalDebt`, plus `statementDate`, `lastPayDate`.
61	
62	Order:
63	1. Card introduction + statement date (glued to the first currency).
64	2. Turkish Lira.
65	3. Dollar, then Euro, then Sterling (only the ones with debt).
66	4. One sentence for the currencies with no debt.
67	5. Remaining auto-payment amount, when there is one (**TBD**, see §9).
68	6. Due date.
69	7. If the caller has more eligible cards: “Başka bir kartınızın borcunu öğrenmek ister misiniz?”
70	8. Offer (§5).
71	
72	Card introduction, example on the Lira line:
73	“Sonu dört iki beş üç ile biten Yıldız Premium kartınıza ait 21 Ağustos 2026 tarihinde kesilen ekstre Türk Lirası borcunuz …”
74	
75	### Turkish Lira: three cases by what has been paid
76	
77	| Paid so far | Sentence |
78	|---|---|
79	| Nothing | “Türk Lirası borcunuz XXX TL, ödenmesi gereken minimum tutar ZZZ TL'dir.” |
80	| Minimum or more | “Türk Lirası borcunuz XXX TL, kalan toplam borcunuz YYY TL'dir. Minimum ödemenizi yaptığınız için teşekkür ederiz.” |
81	| Less than the minimum | “Türk Lirası borcunuz XXX TL, ödenmesi gereken minimum tutar ZZZ TL, kalan toplam borcunuz YYY TL, kalan minimum ödeme tutarınız TTT TL'dir.” |
82	
83	XXX statementDebt, ZZZ minPayment, YYY remainingDebt, TTT remainingMinPayment.
84	How I pick the case (Mert to check): debt only if remainingDebt > 0; "nothing paid" if remainingMinPayment equals or exceeds minPayment; "minimum or more" if remainingMinPayment is zero or below; "less than minimum" otherwise. If remainingDebt is 0,00 we go to the no-debt wording for Lira.
85	
86	No Lira debt → Lira is skipped and goes into the no-debt sentence.
87	
88	### Foreign currencies
89	
90	Same pattern for all three, no paid/unpaid split:
91	
92	“Dolar borcunuz XXX USD, kalan toplam borcunuz YYY USD, ödenmesi gereken minimum tutar ZZZ USD'dir.”
93	Euro and Sterling the same way (EUR, GBP; "İngiliz Sterlini borcunuz …").
94	
95	### Currencies without debt
96	
97	One sentence at the end. My table (not all 15 lines yet, I'll fill the rest):
98	
99	| TL | USD | EUR | GBP | Sentence |
100	|---|---|---|---|---|
101	| debt | – | – | debt | “Dolar ve Euro borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
102	| debt | debt | – | – | “Euro ve İngiliz Sterlini borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
103	| debt | – | debt | – | “Dolar ve İngiliz Sterlini borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
104	| – | debt | debt | debt | “TL borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
105	| – | debt | – | – | “TL, Euro ve İngiliz Sterlini borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
106	| – | – | debt | – | “TL, Dolar ve İngiliz Sterlini borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
107	| debt | debt | debt | debt | nothing, all four are read |
108	| … | | | | TBD |
109	
110	Negative amounts (credit balance) and zero count as "no debt" in that currency. A currency the card does not carry at all: **TBD** whether it goes into this sentence.
111	
112	### Due date
113	
114	“Borçlarınız için son ödeme tarihiniz 16 Eylül 2026'dır.” (date from lastPayDate)
115	
116	If the due date is today, say "bugün": “Borçlarınız için son ödeme tarihiniz bugündür.”
117	
118	### No statement debt
119	
120	“Sonu [son 4 hane] ile biten [kart adı] kartınızın [hesap kesim tarihi] tarihli ekstresinden borcunuz bulunmamaktadır. Gelecek dönemler dahil toplam borcunuz GGG TL'dir. Son ödeme tarihiniz [son ödeme tarihi] olacaktır.”
121	
122	Then the other-card question if there is another eligible card. Otherwise main menu. (Kerem: do we offer e-mail/statement week here too? I lean no, nothing to send.)
123	
124	### How things are spoken
125	
126	- Amounts: lira and kuruş in full ("bir milyon iki yüz otuz dört bin beş yüz altmış yedi lira seksen dokuz kuruş"); zero kuruş is dropped ("iki bin beş yüz Türk Lirası"). Dollar/Euro decimals as cents, Sterling as pence.
127	- Dates: day, month name, year ("21 Ağustos 2026").
128	- Last four digits one by one: "dört iki beş üç", "bir sıfır sıfır üç". Never "kırk iki elli üç", never "çift sıfır".
129	- The full card number is never said.
130	- Every amount and date exactly as the service gave it. Nothing the service did not return is said (no guessing of rates, dates or addresses).
131	
132	## 5. The offer
133	
134	After the due date (and after the other-card question when it applies):
135	
136	“Hesap kesim tarihinizi değiştirebilirim ya da ekstrenizi kayıtlı mail adresinize gönderebilirim.”
137	
138	Only what the caller can actually do is offered:
139	- no registered e-mail → only the statement week ("Hesap kesim tarihinizi değiştirebilirim.");
140	- statement week cannot be changed → only the e-mail;
141	- neither → no offer.
142	
143	That means the contact lookup (`contact.email.get`) has to run before the offer, not after the caller picks e-mail. Mert, OK?
144	
145	**TBD:** we have no way to know in advance whether the caller may still change the week (see §6.2).
146	
147	Answers:
148	
149	| Caller says | Goes to |
150	|---|---|
151	| e-mail | §6.1 |
152	| change statement date / week | §6.2 |
153	| no / nothing else / thanks, bye | main menu, “Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.” |
154	| wants to pay | agent, “Borç ödeme işleminiz için sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum.” |
155	| debt + e-mail in the same sentence | read the debt, then go straight to e-mail without the offer question |
156	
157	## 6. Actions
158	
159	### 6.1 Statement by e-mail
160	
161	Only to the address the bank holds. The assistant never takes an address from the caller.
162	
163	1. `contact.email.get` (customer number). Empty address, or only a phone registered → no suitable e-mail. If the caller asks anyway: “Bankamızda kayıtlı bir e-posta adresiniz bulunmadığı için ekstrenizi gönderemiyorum.” Then statement week if possible, else main menu.
164	2. Read the address back and ask: “Ekstrenizi … adresine göndermemi ister misiniz?” Readable addresses as they are; long or odd ones shortened ("m ile başlayan Gmail adresiniz"), no spelling letter by letter.
165	3. Only on a clear yes: `statement.pdf.send` with card, customer number, the registered address and the statement date.
166	4. “Ekstreniz kayıtlı e-posta adresinize gönderildi.” then “Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.”
167	
168	Other answers:
169	- No → nothing sent, main menu.
170	- "That address is wrong / I don't use it anymore" → nothing sent; it cannot be changed here; main menu.
171	- "Send it to another address" → only the registered address is possible.
172	- "Send last month's" → only the last closed statement.
173	- Sending again in the same call: max three, then main menu.

# Statement debt: self-service step for the voice assistant

Business analysis, working draft
Author: Selin Aydın (Card Self-Service, Freya Bank)
Date: 2 September 2026
Shared with: Kerem Yalçın, Burcu Tan, Mert Koç (for the service part)

> Kerem, Burcu: this is my first pass after the two walkthroughs of the phone menu. Comments inline please, I'll collect them before we sit down with the Freya team. Anything marked **TBD** I could not close myself.

---

## 0. In one paragraph

Today the menu plays a fixed announcement and that's it. With the assistant we want a short conversation instead: which card, how much is owed and by when, and then two things the caller can get done without waiting for an agent (statement PDF by mail, a different statement week). Paying stays with the agents for now. Whatever else the caller brings up, we hand back to the main menu.

## 1. Scope

In:
- Debt reading for one card at a time, all four currencies we carry (Lira, Dollar, Euro, Sterling), with the due date. When the closed statement is fully paid, the "no debt" wording plus the running total.
- The two follow-ups: mailing the statement (only ever to the address we hold) and moving the statement week.
- Choosing the card, where needed.

Out (first list, Kerem please extend):
- Paying the debt itself: handed to an agent.
- Disputes, "I paid but it doesn't show" (agent, see §7).
- Limits, cash advance, card blocking, anything about debit cards.
- Changing the e-mail address.
- Statements of earlier periods.

Burcu thinks statement debt is one of the top three menu choices; she'll try to get a figure.

## 2. How the caller arrives

The phone menu has already identified and authenticated the caller before the hand-over. The assistant receives the customer number with the call and does not run any identity check of its own.

**TBD:** the flow drawing we got from the vendor side has a box "second factor may be needed". I don't see why for a read-only step plus two low-risk actions; to confirm with Elçin.

## 3. Picking the card

The card list comes from `cards.list` (customer number in, eligible credit cards out). Then:

| Situation | What the assistant does |
|---|---|
| Caller already named the card when arriving | If the name fits exactly one card, no selection question. |
| Several cards | Asks which one, with at most two example names taken from the caller's own cards: “Hangi kartınızın borcunu öğrenmek istersiniz? Örneğin, Yıldız Premium veya Yıldız Pratik diyebilirsiniz.” |
| Caller asks for "all my cards" | Not possible, the debt service takes one card at a time. Selection question again (counts as a failed attempt). |
| Name not on the list | Tells the caller there is no card with that name and reads the eligible ones again. |
| Two or more cards with the same name | Asks for the last four digits: “Yıldız isimli birden fazla kartınız var. Kartınızın son dört hanesini söyler misiniz?” (name of the card in place of "Yıldız") |
| Same name and same last four | Asks for the full card number: “Son dört hanesi aynı olan birden fazla kartınız var. Kart numaranızın tamamını söyler misiniz?” |

Two easy cases outside the table: a single card is simply taken, no question. No eligible card at all: “Ekstre borcunu sorgulayabileceğiniz uygun bir kredi kartınız bulunmuyor. Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.”

Notes:
- Digits can come as "dört iki beş üç", "kırk iki elli üç" etc. The assistant maps them to the four digits and moves on. No reading back of the digits, no "… kartınızla devam ediyorum" confirmation; the card name is said anyway at the start of the debt reading.
- Supplementary card holders: they see no eligible card of their own here. Tell them and ask for a different card. (Burcu, is that what the menu does today?)
- If the card name comes back empty from the service, introduce the card by its last four only.

## 4. Reading the debt

Service: `cards.balance` with the chosen card. It returns one block per currency (`debtTL`, `debtUSD`, `debtEUR`, `debtGBP`) with `statementDebt`, `minPayment`, `remainingDebt`, `remainingMinPayment`, `totalDebt`, plus `statementDate`, `lastPayDate`.

Order:
1. Card introduction + statement date (glued to the first currency).
2. Turkish Lira.
3. Dollar, then Euro, then Sterling (only the ones with debt).
4. One sentence for the currencies with no debt.
5. Remaining auto-payment amount, when there is one (**TBD**, see §9).
6. Due date.
7. If the caller has more eligible cards: “Başka bir kartınızın borcunu öğrenmek ister misiniz?”
8. Offer (§5).

Card introduction, example on the Lira line:
“Sonu dört iki beş üç ile biten Yıldız Premium kartınıza ait 21 Ağustos 2026 tarihinde kesilen ekstre Türk Lirası borcunuz …”

### Turkish Lira: three cases by what has been paid

| Paid so far | Sentence |
|---|---|
| Nothing | “Türk Lirası borcunuz XXX TL, ödenmesi gereken minimum tutar ZZZ TL'dir.” |
| Minimum or more | “Türk Lirası borcunuz XXX TL, kalan toplam borcunuz YYY TL'dir. Minimum ödemenizi yaptığınız için teşekkür ederiz.” |
| Less than the minimum | “Türk Lirası borcunuz XXX TL, ödenmesi gereken minimum tutar ZZZ TL, kalan toplam borcunuz YYY TL, kalan minimum ödeme tutarınız TTT TL'dir.” |

XXX statementDebt, ZZZ minPayment, YYY remainingDebt, TTT remainingMinPayment.
How I pick the case (Mert to check): debt only if remainingDebt > 0; "nothing paid" if remainingMinPayment equals or exceeds minPayment; "minimum or more" if remainingMinPayment is zero or below; "less than minimum" otherwise. If remainingDebt is 0,00 we go to the no-debt wording for Lira.

No Lira debt → Lira is skipped and goes into the no-debt sentence.

### Foreign currencies

Same pattern for all three, no paid/unpaid split:

“Dolar borcunuz XXX USD, kalan toplam borcunuz YYY USD, ödenmesi gereken minimum tutar ZZZ USD'dir.”
Euro and Sterling the same way (EUR, GBP; "İngiliz Sterlini borcunuz …").

### Currencies without debt

One sentence at the end. My table (not all 15 lines yet, I'll fill the rest):

| TL | USD | EUR | GBP | Sentence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| debt | – | – | debt | “Dolar ve Euro borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
| debt | debt | – | – | “Euro ve İngiliz Sterlini borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
| debt | – | debt | – | “Dolar ve İngiliz Sterlini borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
| – | debt | debt | debt | “TL borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
| – | debt | – | – | “TL, Euro ve İngiliz Sterlini borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
| – | – | debt | – | “TL, Dolar ve İngiliz Sterlini borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
| debt | debt | debt | debt | nothing, all four are read |
| … | | | | TBD |

Negative amounts (credit balance) and zero count as "no debt" in that currency. A currency the card does not carry at all: **TBD** whether it goes into this sentence.

### Due date

“Borçlarınız için son ödeme tarihiniz 16 Eylül 2026'dır.” (date from lastPayDate)

If the due date is today, say "bugün": “Borçlarınız için son ödeme tarihiniz bugündür.”

### No statement debt

“Sonu [son 4 hane] ile biten [kart adı] kartınızın [hesap kesim tarihi] tarihli ekstresinden borcunuz bulunmamaktadır. Gelecek dönemler dahil toplam borcunuz GGG TL'dir. Son ödeme tarihiniz [son ödeme tarihi] olacaktır.”

Then the other-card question if there is another eligible card. Otherwise main menu. (Kerem: do we offer e-mail/statement week here too? I lean no, nothing to send.)

### How things are spoken

- Amounts: lira and kuruş in full ("bir milyon iki yüz otuz dört bin beş yüz altmış yedi lira seksen dokuz kuruş"); zero kuruş is dropped ("iki bin beş yüz Türk Lirası"). Dollar/Euro decimals as cents, Sterling as pence.
- Dates: day, month name, year ("21 Ağustos 2026").
- Last four digits one by one: "dört iki beş üç", "bir sıfır sıfır üç". Never "kırk iki elli üç", never "çift sıfır".
- The full card number is never said.
- Every amount and date exactly as the service gave it. Nothing the service did not return is said (no guessing of rates, dates or addresses).

## 5. The offer

After the due date (and after the other-card question when it applies):

“Hesap kesim tarihinizi değiştirebilirim ya da ekstrenizi kayıtlı mail adresinize gönderebilirim.”

Only what the caller can actually do is offered:
- no registered e-mail → only the statement week ("Hesap kesim tarihinizi değiştirebilirim.");
- statement week cannot be changed → only the e-mail;
- neither → no offer.

That means the contact lookup (`contact.email.get`) has to run before the offer, not after the caller picks e-mail. Mert, OK?

**TBD:** we have no way to know in advance whether the caller may still change the week (see §6.2).

Answers:

| Caller says | Goes to |
|---|---|
| e-mail | §6.1 |
| change statement date / week | §6.2 |
| no / nothing else / thanks, bye | main menu, “Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.” |
| wants to pay | agent, “Borç ödeme işleminiz için sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum.” |
| debt + e-mail in the same sentence | read the debt, then go straight to e-mail without the offer question |

## 6. Actions

### 6.1 Statement by e-mail

Only to the address the bank holds. The assistant never takes an address from the caller.

1. `contact.email.get` (customer number). Empty address, or only a phone registered → no suitable e-mail. If the caller asks anyway: “Bankamızda kayıtlı bir e-posta adresiniz bulunmadığı için ekstrenizi gönderemiyorum.” Then statement week if possible, else main menu.
2. Read the address back and ask: “Ekstrenizi … adresine göndermemi ister misiniz?” Readable addresses as they are; long or odd ones shortened ("m ile başlayan Gmail adresiniz"), no spelling letter by letter.
3. Only on a clear yes: `statement.pdf.send` with card, customer number, the registered address and the statement date.
4. “Ekstreniz kayıtlı e-posta adresinize gönderildi.” then “Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.”

Other answers:
- No → nothing sent, main menu.
- "That address is wrong / I don't use it anymore" → nothing sent; it cannot be changed here; main menu.
- "Send it to another address" → only the registered address is possible.
- "Send last month's" → only the last closed statement.
- Sending again in the same call: max three, then main menu.
- Service error → “Şu anda işleminizi gerçekleştiremiyorum, sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum.”

### 6.2 Changing the statement week

Services: `statement.week.get` (current), `statement.week.decide` (preview, changes nothing), `statement.week.change` (the change).

1. Current state: “[kart adı] kartınızın hesap kesim tarihi her ayın [hafta]. haftası olarak tanımlı. Bir sonraki hesap kesim tarihiniz [tarih], son ödeme tarihiniz [tarih]. Hesap kesim tarihinizi değiştirmek ister misiniz?” No → main menu.
   Joint statement: also read the main and the linked card (names, week, next closing and due dates).
2. Options, without the current week: “Hesap kesim tarihinizi ayın 1., 3. ya da 4. haftasına alabilirim. Hangisini tercih edersiniz?”
   - A week or a date we didn't offer → only the offered weeks; read them again.
   - The current week → no change needed.
3. Preview with the chosen week and the current statement day.
4. Confirm: “Yeni hesap kesim haftanız her ayın 3. haftası olacak. Yeni hesap kesim tarihiniz [tarih], son ödeme tarihiniz [tarih] olacak. Onaylıyor musunuz?”
   Joint statement: after the question, add “Bu değişiklik kartınıza bağlı [bağlı kart adı] kartınızı da etkileyecek.”
   - Only a clear "evet" counts. "Olabilir", "sanırım" → ask once more, clearly (three tries).
   - No → no change, “Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.”
5. `statement.week.change`, only after preview + clear yes.
6. “Sonu [son 4 hane] ile biten [kart adı] kartınızın hesap kesim haftası her ayın 3. haftası olarak değiştirildi. Yeni hesap kesim tarihiniz [tarih], son ödeme tarihiniz [tarih].” Dates from the preview (the change call does not return them). Then main menu.

Any of the three services fails → “Şu anda hesap kesim tarihinizi değiştiremiyorum, sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum.”

How often a caller may change: **TBD**. Burcu says the menu has its own limits today; I need the exact rule and whether any service tells us beforehand.

## 7. Exits and general behaviour

| When | Where | Sentence |
|---|---|---|
| Done / nothing else / goodbye after the reading | Main menu | “Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.” |
| Caller asks for something else mid-flow | Main menu, the request is passed on | “Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.” |

| Caller speaks another language | Main menu | “Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.” |

1 # Test environment: synthetic customers 2 3 Prepared by Mert Koç (Integration Architecture), 1 October 2026. Goes with `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md`. 4 5 Everyone below is made up: names, customer numbers, card numbers and addresses exist only in the test environment. The full answers of every service for every customer are in `test-customers.json`. If you write a mock, serve exactly those bodies with exactly those status codes; this page is only the overview. 6 7 ## How the JSON is laid out 8 9 `customers` is the customer list. Each customer has `customerNo`, `firstName`, `lastName` and `services`. Under `services` there is one entry per service, and at the bottom of each entry an object with `http` (status code) and `response` (body to return). 10 11 How to find the right answer for a request: 12 13 | Service | Look up by | Remarks | 14 |---|---|---| 15 | `cards.list` | `data.customerNo` | one answer per customer | 16 | `cards.balance` | `data.cardNumber` | the masked number exactly as `cards.list` gave it | 17 | `statement.week.get` | `data.cardNumber` | | 18 | `statement.week.decide` | `data.cardNumber`, then `data.newStatementWeek` (`"1"`..`"4"`) | the card's current week has no entry | 19 | `statement.week.change` | `data.cardNumber`, then `data.newStatementWeek` | the card's current week has no entry | 20 | `contact.email.get` | `data.customerNo` | one answer per customer; `intAddressInfoType` doesn't change it | 21 | `statement.pdf.send` | `data.customerNo` | one answer per customer; a few customers have no entry at all | 22 23 - `customerNo` can arrive as `"90000001"` or `90000001`, and `newStatementWeek` as `3` or `"3"`. Treat them the same. 24 - One entry also has `delaySeconds` next to `http` and `response`: wait that many seconds, then answer with `response`. Don't put the field in the body. 25 - No entry for the customer or card (or for that week): return the 404 of that service from section 4 of the contract; where the contract has no 404 for the service, a 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR` body. # Mock service with Cloudflare Workers

Your flow's tools call a mock service that you write, instead of the real bank service. You publish this service as a free Cloudflare Worker. The `example/` folder here only shows the pattern: a Worker with a single endpoint (`POST /ping`). You will write the statement-debt services yourself.

## Requirements

- Node.js 18 or later
- A free Cloudflare account (dash.cloudflare.com)
- Wrangler (Cloudflare's command-line tool): runs without installing, via `npx wrangler ...`

## 1. Run the example locally

```bash
cd example
npx wrangler dev
```

The Worker opens at `http://localhost:8787`. Try it from another terminal:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8787/ping \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"kod": "A1"}'
```

The response is the same as `example/example-response.json`. For a code that does not exist it returns `404` and `{"hata": "kayıt bulunamadı"}`.

## 2. Publish it

```bash
npx wrangler login      # grant access to your Cloudflare account in the browser
npx wrangler deploy
```

The output shows the Worker address: `https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev`. To change the name, change the `name` field in `wrangler.toml`. Run `npx wrangler deploy` again whenever the code changes; the address stays the same.

Check after publishing:

```bash
curl -s https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/health
```

## 3. Connect the tool in the Freya flow to the Worker

1. Add an API tool to the flow.
2. Enter the method and address: `POST https://<your-worker-name>.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/<path>`. For the statement services, use the same path as under the bank's base address in `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` (for example `/voice/v1/cards.list`).
3. In the request body, write variables in the form `{{variable_name}}`. Example: `{"data": {"customerNo": "{{customerNumber}}", "aiFlow": "..."}, "call": {...}}`. During the call, the variable's value is substituted in.
4. Take the fields you will use in the flow from the response into variables.

The "Test API Request" button in the panel may send the text `{{customerNumber}}` as is, without filling in the variables. In this case the example Worker returns a valid record instead of an error (`isTemplateVariable`). Doing the same in your own services makes testing easier.

## When writing your own services

- Endpoints, request and response fields must match `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` exactly: the same path, the same field names (`data`/`call` request body, `data`/`result` response), the same date and amount format. The test customers' responses are in `../test-environment/test-customers.json`, explained in `../test-environment/test-customers.md`.
- Keep customer and card data in a table inside the Worker file (like `RECORDS` in the example). No database is needed.
- For a customer or card that is not found, return the error response from the contract; do not return made-up data.
- Responses should return data only (amount, date, status). The flow builds the sentence to be said to the customer.
- Do not put secret keys or real personal data in it; the Worker address is public.

content.content:
1	# Tools and code
2	
3	This page describes how a workflow calls HTTP APIs and runs Python. Read [workflow-format.md](workflow-format.md) first.
4	
5	Statements marked "verified in a working builder" come from a builder that created a 6-node workflow through the REST API. The workflow has code nodes, `api_call` tools, post-hooks and transitions on tool results. Its agent passed its practice cases. Statements marked "seen in a trial call" come from the event log of a simulation call made with that builder.
6	
7	## Tool function shape
8	
9	Every external action is a **tool function**. The shape is the same wherever you attach it.
10	
11	```json
12	{
13	  "type": "function",
14	  "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 2 },
15	  "function": {
16	    "name": "lookup_order",
17	    "handler": "__function__:api_call",
18	    "description": "Look up one order. CALL it when the caller asks about a specific order.",
19	    "parameters": {
20	      "type": "object",
21	      "properties": {
22	        "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/orders/lookup" },
23	        "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
24	        "headers": {
25	          "type": "object",
26	          "properties": { "Content-Type": { "type": "string", "default": "application/json" } }
27	        },
28	        "body": {
29	          "type": "object",
30	          "properties": {
31	            "customer_id": { "type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}" },
32	            "order_number": { "type": "string", "description": "Order number, digits only", "default": "{{order_number}}" }
33	          },
34	          "required": ["order_number"]
35	        }
36	      }
37	    }
38	  },
39	  "response_mapping": [
40	    { "path": "data.status", "variable": "order_status" }
41	  ]
42	}
43	```
44	
45	| Field | Meaning |
46	|---|---|
47	| `type` | Always `"function"` |
48	| `function.name` | Tool name. The model calls it by this name. Result variables are named after it |
49	| `function.handler` | Which runtime executes the tool. See the table below |
50	| `function.description` | Read by the dialogue model when the tool is in `tools`. Ignored in `pre_actions` |
51	| `function.parameters` | JSON-schema object. `properties` holds the parameters |
52	| `config.timeoutMs` | Timeout of one attempt, in milliseconds |
53	| `config.maxRetries` | Tool-level retries of a failed call |
54	| `config.interruptible` | `false` makes the tool run in the background. See "Background tools" |
55	| `config.alwaysRunsAt` | Makes the tool a lifecycle tool. See "Lifecycle tools" |
56	| `response_mapping` | Tool level, for tools in `tools`. Maps the result to variables |
57	| `pre_process_code` | Python hook that runs before the call |
58	| `post_process_code` | Python hook that runs after the call |
59	
60	| Handler | Runs |
61	|---|---|
62	| `__function__:api_call` | An HTTP request |
63	| `__function__:code_exec` | A Python snippet in a sandbox |
64	| `__function__:end_call` | Hangs up. Used in the `terminal` of an `end_call` node |
65	
66	Handlers for integrations, knowledge search, call transfer and rescheduling also exist. They are not needed here.
67	
68	`api_call` parameters:
69	
70	| Parameter | Meaning |
71	|---|---|
72	| `url` | Request URL. `{{var}}` works |
73	| `method` | HTTP method |
74	| `headers` | Object. Each header is a property with a `default` |
75	| `body` | Object. Each body field is a property under `body.properties` |
76	| `connect_retries` | Transport retries. See "Retries and timeouts" |
77	
78	## How a parameter gets its value
79	
80	One key decides, per parameter: `default`.
81	
82	| Declaration | Who supplies the value | Does the model see the parameter |
83	|---|---|---|
84	| `default` with a literal, or with a `{{var}}` that has a value | The workflow. The value is **baked** | No |
85	| `default` with a `{{var}}` that has no value when the node is entered | The model | Yes, named after the variable, with the property's `type`, `description` and `enum` |
86	| no `default` | The model | Yes |
87	| `const` | Nobody. `const` does **not** bake | It only constrains the model's own output |
88	
89	Rules:
90	
91	- **Use `default` for fixed backend config** such as `url`, `method` and auth headers. At registration the engine moves every `default` into the tool's base config, resolves `{{var}}` from the variable table, and removes the field from the schema the model sees.
92	- **Never use `const` for a value you want sent.** The engine reads only `default`. A `{{var}}` inside a `const` never resolves. An `api_call` whose `url` is a `const` fails with "URL is required".
93	- **Baking happens when the node is entered.** A `{{var}}` default is resolved against the variable table at that moment.
94	
95	The working builder uses this for every tool: `customer_id` has `"default": "{{customer_id}}"` and is baked from a call variable. Every other body field has `"default": "{{<field name>}}"`, where no variable of that name exists, so the model fills it. Verified in a working builder.
96	
97	Seen in a trial call: the model's arguments are stored as `<tool>_args.<field>` in the variable table, for example `lookup_order_args.order_number`. They were not stored under the bare field name.
98	
99	Take care that a model-filled field does not share its name with a variable that is already set when the node is entered. The value would be baked and the model would never see the parameter.
100	
101	### `api_call` body field rules
102	
103	- Declare each body field as a leaf under `body.properties.<field>`.
104	- Put the field's `type`, `description` and `enum` on that leaf. Put required fields in `body.required`.
105	- Give each leaf its own `default`.
106	- Do not put a field spec at the top level of `parameters.properties` next to a `body.default` template object. The engine looks for the spec at `body.properties.<field>`, does not find it, and the model sees only "Template variable: name". The `enum` and `description` are lost while the call still works.
107	- A body that exists only as one `body.default` object also shows as an empty form in the dashboard editor. Saving from there removes the tool.
108	
109	A `code_exec` tool is different: its parameters are true top-level arguments. Declare a model-filled one as a top-level property without `default`.
110	
111	### When a baked variable has no value
112	
113	| Field type | Variable unset | Variable is `""` |
114	|---|---|---|
115	| Normal field in an engine-run call (`pre_actions`, lifecycle tool) | The field is dropped from the request. No error | The field is sent empty |
116	| `code` of `code_exec` | The literal text `{{var}}` stays in the Python source and the snippet crashes | |
117	
118	Fix: make sure an earlier node always sets the variable, even to a sentinel value. In code, read variables from `vars` and do not splice them in with `{{var}}`.
119	
120	### Constrain model-filled parameters
121	
122	When a value must be one of a known set, do not use a free string. The model sometimes invents a value that looks plausible.
123	
124	- Use an `enum` on the leaf, and list the values in the `description` as well.
125	- Or use a `number` that is an index into a list, with the valid range in the description. A pre-hook or the backend turns the index into the real value.
126	- If neither is possible, name the exact source in the description and tell the model to copy the value unchanged.
127	
128	```json
129	{
130	  "type": "object",
131	  "properties": {
132	    "queue": {
133	      "type": "string",
134	      "description": "Team that takes over. One of: billing, delivery, returns.",
135	      "enum": ["billing", "delivery", "returns"],
136	      "default": "{{queue}}"
137	    }
138	  },
139	  "required": ["queue"]
140	}
141	```
142	
143	## `pre_actions` versus `tools`
144	
145	The placement decides who fires the call.
146	
147	| Placement | Node type | Who calls it | When |
148	|---|---|---|---|
149	| `pre_actions` | `api_request`, `code` | The engine | On node entry, before any model turn |
150	| `tools` | `conversation` | The dialogue model | During a turn, when the model decides to |
151	| Workflow-level `tools` with `config.alwaysRunsAt` | none | The engine | At call start or call end |
152	
153	The platform removes `tools` from non-conversation nodes and `pre_actions` from conversation nodes. It does so without an error: the JSON you sent looks fine, the create call succeeds, and the stored node has an empty array. A node cannot use both.
154	
155	**Use `pre_actions`** when the call must always run and the model has nothing to decide. Example: after the order number is known, always fetch the order.
156	
157	**Use `tools`** when the call depends on what the user says. Example: cancel the order only if the caller asks for it.
158	
159	Differences in behaviour:
160	
161	| | `pre_actions` | `tools` |
162	|---|---|---|
163	| Can be skipped | No | Yes. The model may not call it if the description and the prompt do not push for it |
164	| Timing | Node entry | Inside a turn. The model can call a tool, speak, then call another |
165	| Result in the conversation | A tool call and tool result pair is added to the history | The same |
166	| `response_mapping` lives | On the **node** | On the **tool** |
167	| `description` | Ignored | The only text the model reads about the tool |
168	
169	To run a fixed call before a tool-driven conversation, use a passthrough `api_request` node and transition from it into the conversation node. Do not build a long chain of passthrough nodes for optional actions. Put those into one conversation node with several tools.
170	
171	### A `pre_actions` node
172	
173	```json
174	{
175	  "name": "fetch_order",
176	  "node_type": "api_request",
177	  "passthrough": true,
178	  "passthrough_default_transition": "present",
179	  "on_enter": { "type": "silent" },
180	  "pre_actions": [
181	    {
182	      "type": "function",
183	      "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 2 },
184	      "function": {
185	        "name": "get_order",
186	        "handler": "__function__:api_call",
187	        "description": "Get the order.",
188	        "parameters": {
189	          "type": "object",
190	          "properties": {
191	            "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/get_order" },
192	            "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
193	            "headers": { "type": "object", "properties": { "Content-Type": { "type": "string", "default": "application/json" } } },
194	            "body": { "type": "object", "properties": { "order_number": { "type": "string", "default": "{{order_number}}" } }, "required": [] }
195	          }
196	        }
197	      }
198	    }
199	  ],
200	  "response_mapping": [
201	    { "path": "data.items", "variable": "items" }
202	  ],
203	  "transitions": [
204	    { "target_node": "present", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
205	  ]
206	}
207	```
208	
209	The last `always` transition is mandatory. A passthrough node with no matching transition deadlocks.
210	
211	### Tool descriptions
212	
213	In `tools`, the `description` decides whether the model calls the tool.
214	
215	- Write it as an instruction with the trigger: "CALL it every time the caller gives an order number."
216	- A plain description such as "Looks up an order" lets the model acknowledge the request in words and never call the tool. That is the most common failure of nodes with many tools.
217	- If two tools could match, say which one not to use and name the other.
218	- In `task_message`, put the tool rules before long reference text and state: when a rule says to use a tool, call the tool.
219	- The working builder also tells the model to call one tool per message and to speak after every tool result. Verified in a working builder. In a trial call a model turn with no text and no tool call produced the error event "The model returned no speakable content".
220	
221	A tool is available only in the nodes that list it. Seen in a trial call: the model called a tool that the current node did not list. The result was the text "The function `<name>` is not currently available."
222	
223	## `response_mapping`
224	
225	`response_mapping` copies values from a call result into named variables. It needs no model call.
226	
227	```json
228	{
229	  "response_mapping": [
230	    { "path": "data.status", "variable": "order_status" },
231	    { "path": "data.items", "variable": "items" }
232	  ]
233	}
234	```
235	
236	| Field | Meaning |
237	|---|---|
238	| `path` | Dot path into the tool result |
239	| `variable` | Name of the variable to set |
240	
241	### Placement
242	
243	- For a tool in `tools`: inside the tool object, next to `function` and `config`.
244	- For `pre_actions`: at the **node level**. A `response_mapping` nested inside a `pre_actions` entry is ignored and the variable never appears.
245	
246	`extraction_schema` follows the same placement rule if you use it on a call result.
247	
248	### Where a result lands (trial findings)
249	
250	Seen in a trial call: the result of an `api_call` is an envelope around the HTTP response.
251	
252	```json
253	{
254	  "status": "success",
255	  "data": { "ok": true, "verified": true, "attempts_left": 3 },
256	  "message": "Successfully executed POST request",
257	  "status_code": 200,
258	  "header": { "Content-Type": "application/json" }
259	}
260	```
261	
262	`data` is the JSON body the API returned. `header` holds the HTTP response headers.
263	
264	The engine also writes every result into the variable table by itself, flattened with dots. You do not need a mapping for these. For a tool named `check_answer` whose API returned `{"ok": true, "verified": true, "attempts_left": 3}`, the trial call's variable table held:
265	
266	| Variable | Value |
267	|---|---|
268	| `check_answer_args.<field>` | Each argument the model sent |
269	| `check_answer_response.status` | `success` |
270	| `check_answer_response.data.ok` | `true` (a string) |
271	| `check_answer_response.data.verified` | `true` (a string) |
272	| `check_answer_response.data.attempts_left` | `3` |
273	| `check_answer_response.message` | `Successfully executed POST request` |
274	| `check_answer_response.status_code` | `200` |
275	| `check_answer_response.header.<Header-Name>` | One variable per response header |
276	| `check_answer_status_code` | `200` |
277	| `check_answer_success_count` | Number of successful calls so far |
278	
279	Each call of the same tool overwrites the previous `_args` and `_response` values.
280	
281	### Which mapping paths work
282	
283	- **Start the path at the envelope, with `data.`**. If the API returns `{"ok": true}`, map `data.ok`. If it returns `{"products": [...]}`, map `data.products`. Verified in a working builder, on a tool-level mapping and on a node-level mapping.
284	- A path without the `data.` prefix (for the same body: `ok`) is not confirmed. A smaller example builder uses it. In an early trial call the mapped variables stayed unset and the transitions on them never fired. The mapping paths of that call are not recorded. The builder that passed uses `data.` paths.
285	- The flattened key can be used directly as a transition variable: `check_answer_response.data.verified`. Verified in a working builder, which tests the mapped variable and the flattened key in the same OR group as a safeguard.
286	- Booleans arrive as strings. The trial call showed `true` in lower case in the flattened keys. Test both `"true"` and `"True"`, or map a string field.
287	- A mapped list or object: the exact form it has later inside `vars` is not confirmed. The working builder reads it defensively. It accepts a list, a JSON string, and flattened keys.
288	
289	## Routing on tool results
290	
291	Routing runs again after a tool result arrives. A transition on a result variable fires in the same turn, before any further model turn. Seen in a trial call.
292	
293	```json
294	{
295	  "transitions": [
296	    {
297	      "target_node": "load_order",
298	      "description": "The check passed",
299	      "condition": {
300	        "logic": "or",
301	        "conditions": [
302	          { "variable": "check_passed", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true" },
303	          { "variable": "check_passed", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True" },
304	          { "variable": "check_answer_response.data.verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true" },
305	          { "variable": "check_answer_response.data.verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True" }
306	        ]
307	      }
308	    }
309	  ]
310	}
311	```
312	
313	Rules:
314	
315	- On a passthrough node, end with an `always` transition so that a failed or empty response does not deadlock.
316	- Use a tool result to leave a conversation node. The pattern "a closing tool sets a variable, a transition on that variable leads to an `end_call` node" is verified in a working builder.
317	- To leave a node that carries out an action, do not re-test the user's earlier intent with `matches_intent`. The router looks at the latest user message and can route away before the tool was called. Extract a follow-up enum with a default such as `stay`, and branch with `equals`.
318	
319	### Success and failure counters
320	
321	The engine keeps two integer variables per call target. No mapping is needed.
322	
323	| Placement | Variables |
324	|---|---|
325	| `pre_actions` node | `<nodeId>_success_count`, `<nodeId>_failure_count` |
326	| Tool in `tools` with handler `api_call` | `<toolName>_success_count`, `<toolName>_failure_count` |
327	
328	Seen in a trial call: `check_answer_success_count` was `2` after two successful calls, and a code node named `setup` produced `setup_success_count` with the value `1`.
329	
330	```json
331	{
332	  "transitions": [
333	    { "target_node": "give_up", "description": "The lookup failed three times", "condition": { "logic": "or", "conditions": [ { "variable": "lookup_order_failure_count", "operator": "greater_than", "operand": 2 } ] } },
334	    { "target_node": "ask_again", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
335	  ]
336	}
337	```
338	
339	### `suppress_tool_results`
340	
341	A node-level boolean for nodes that run API calls. With `true` the dialogue model sees only a short `{status: "success"}` summary in place of the raw response. Variables are still mapped and routing still sees them. Use it for large responses, or when the mapped variables already hold everything the model needs.
342	
343	### Background tools
344	
345	A tool with `"config": {"interruptible": false}` runs in the background. A user interruption does not cancel it. Its result arrives one or more turns later. The mapped variables, the `_response` keys and the counters are filled as usual, but not in the same turn. A transition that reads them right after the call can find them unset. Gate on the variable with `is_set`.
346	
347	## Retries and timeouts
348	
349	| Setting | Where | Default | What it does |
350	|---|---|---|---|
351	| `timeoutMs` | `config` | not documented | Time limit of one attempt, in milliseconds |
352	| `maxRetries` | `config` | not documented | Tool-level retries after a failed response |
353	| `connect_retries` | `parameters.properties`, as a baked parameter | `2` | Retries when the connection could not be established |
354	| `timeout_ms` | `code_exec` parameter | `30000` | Time limit of a code snippet |
355	
356	`connect_retries` in detail:
357	
358	- It retries only failures to establish the connection: connection refused, or reset during the TCP or TLS handshake. The request never reached the server, so a repeat is safe even for POST.
359	- HTTP error statuses and timeouts are not retried by it.
360	- Hard cap `5`. `0` means a single attempt.
361	- Back-off is 150 ms times the attempt number, with a new connection each time.
362	- All attempts share one 30 second budget for the request.
363	- Declare it next to `url` and `method`: `"connect_retries": {"type": "number", "default": 0}`. It is not a `config` field.
364	
365	The working builder sets `maxRetries` to `0` on tools that write data and to `2` on its read-only `pre_actions` call. A retried write can record the same thing twice if the API is not idempotent.
366	
367	## Pre and post Python hooks
368	
369	An `api_call` tool can carry two Python snippets. They run on the server, in a sandbox, right before and right after the call. They are top-level fields of the tool object.
370	
371	```json
372	{
373	  "type": "function",
374	  "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 0 },
375	  "function": {
376	    "name": "check_answer",
377	    "handler": "__function__:api_call",
378	    "description": "Check one answer. CALL it every time the caller answers the question.",
379	    "parameters": {
380	      "type": "object",
381	      "properties": {
382	        "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/check_answer" },
383	        "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
384	        "body": { "type": "object", "properties": { "answer": { "type": "string", "description": "The caller's answer", "default": "{{answer}}" } }, "required": ["answer"] }
385	      }
386	    }
387	  },
388	  "pre_process_code": "vars['member_code'] = str(vars.get('member_code') or '').strip().upper()",
389	  "post_process_code": "try:\n    if isinstance(result, dict):\n        result.pop('header', None)\n        d = result.get('data')\n        if isinstance(d, dict):\n            d['what_to_do_next'] = 'Ask the next question.' if d.get('verified') else 'Ask the same question again.'\nexcept Exception:\n    pass\n"
390	}
391	```
392	
393	| Hook | Names available | Use |
394	|---|---|---|
395	| `pre_process_code` | `vars`: mutable dict that fills the `{{var}}` placeholders of the request. `config`: the substituted request with `url`, `method`, `headers`, `body` | Clean a value, or rewrite the whole request |
396	| `post_process_code` | `result`: the tool result, mutable | Reshape, shorten or extend the result |
397	
398	Documented behaviour:
399	
400	- The post-hook runs before `response_mapping` and extraction see the result.
401	- An empty or whitespace-only string means no hook.
402	- Hooks are honoured only on `api_call` tools (and on the integration and knowledge search handlers). The platform removes them from any other handler when the workflow is saved.
403	- In a pre-hook, setting `config['body']` to a string sends that string as the raw body, with no JSON encoding. Set the `Content-Type` header yourself in that case.
404	
405	### What `result` looks like in a post-hook
406	
407	The internal reference shows `result` as the response body. A working builder shows otherwise. Verified in a working builder:
408	
409	- For an `api_call`, `result` is the envelope described above: a dict with `status`, `data`, `message`, `status_code` and `header`. The API's JSON body is `result["data"]`.
410	- A key that the hook adds inside `result["data"]` reaches the dialogue model as part of the tool result. The working builder adds a `what_to_do_next` sentence there, and its prompt tells the model to obey it.
411	- `result.pop("header", None)` removes the response headers. The working builder does this on every tool, so that headers do not take up space in the model's context.
412	- Mapping paths still start with `data.` when a post-hook is present.
413	
414	The working builder writes every hook inside `try` and `except Exception: pass` and checks types with `isinstance` before use. What the platform does when a hook raises is not documented.
415	
416	Seen in a test on 10 October: a post-hook can read call variables and write new variables, and a later pre-hook reads them. Not confirmed: whether a change to `result` also changes the flattened `<tool>_response.*` variables.
417	
418	## Code nodes and `code_exec`
419	
420	A `code` node runs a Python snippet when it is entered. The snippet is a `code_exec` function in `pre_actions`.
421	
422	```json
423	{
424	  "name": "compute_delivery",
425	  "node_type": "code",
426	  "passthrough": true,
427	  "passthrough_default_transition": "tell_delivery",
428	  "on_enter": { "type": "silent" },
429	  "pre_actions": [
430	    {
431	      "type": "function",
432	      "function": {
433	        "name": "code_exec",
434	        "handler": "__function__:code_exec",
435	        "parameters": {
436	          "type": "object",
437	          "properties": {
438	            "code": { "type": "string", "default": "import datetime\ntry:\n    start = datetime.date.fromisoformat(str(vars.get('shipped_on'))[:10])\n    eta = start + datetime.timedelta(days=3)\n    vars['delivery_day'] = eta.isoformat()\n    vars['delivery_state'] = 'known'\nexcept Exception:\n    vars['delivery_day'] = ''\n    vars['delivery_state'] = 'unknown'\n" },
439	            "timeout_ms": { "type": "number", "default": 10000 }
440	          }
441	        }
442	      }
443	    }
444	  ],
445	  "transitions": [
446	    { "target_node": "tell_delivery", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
447	  ]
448	}
449	```
450	
451	| Parameter | Meaning |
452	|---|---|
453	| `code` | The Python source, as a baked `default` string |
454	| `timeout_ms` | Time limit in milliseconds. Default `30000` |
455	
456	### Reading and writing variables
457	
458	- The snippet gets a dict named `vars`. It holds the current workflow variables.
459	- Read with `vars.get("name")`. A variable that was never set is absent.
460	- Write with `vars["name"] = value`. Every key the snippet assigns becomes a workflow variable.
461	
462	Verified in a working builder:
463	
464	- Call variables are in `vars`. The builder reads `vars.get("now")`, a call variable passed with the simulation.
465	- The result of an earlier `api_request` node is reachable from `vars` in a later code node. The builder looks for it under the mapped variable name first and under the flattened result keys second. Which of the two held the data is not recorded.
466	- A string written to `vars["date_facts"]` in a code node resolves as `{{date_facts}}` in the `task_message` of later conversation nodes. Multi-line strings work.
467	- The standard modules `json`, `re` and `datetime` can be imported.
468	- The same snippet can run in two code nodes at different points of the call. The later run sees the variables added in between.
469	
470	### What a code node returns
471	
472	Seen in a trial call: the result of a successful `code_exec` is
473	
474	```json
475	{ "status": "success", "data": null, "message": "Code executed successfully", "status_code": 200 }
476	```
477	
478	The snippet's output is not in `data`. Its values reach the workflow only through `vars`. After a code node named `setup` ran, the variable table held:
479	
480	| Variable | Value |
481	|---|---|
482	| each key the snippet wrote, for example `date_facts` | the value, with source `tool_result` and source node `setup` |
483	| `setup_response.status` | `success` |
484	| `setup_response.data` | `null` |
485	| `setup_response.message` | `Code executed successfully` |
486	| `setup_response.status_code` | `200` |
487	| `setup_status_code` | `200` |
488	| `setup_success_count` | `1` |
489	
490	For a code node the automatic keys are named after the **node**, not after `code_exec`.
491	
492	### Rules for snippets
493	
494	- **Do not write `{{` or `}}` in the code.** The internal sources disagree on whether the `code` field is templated. One says it is exempt. Another says placeholders are resolved when the code runs and an unset one is left as literal text, which breaks the Python. The working builder removes every `{{` and `}}` from generated code (a nested dict literal such as `{'a': {'b': 1}}` ends in `}}`) and reads all values from `vars`.
495	- **Never let a snippet raise.** Wrap the body in `try` and `except`, and write a fallback value for every variable that a later prompt or condition reads. A prompt that references an unset variable shows the literal placeholder to the model.
496	- **Write strings for routing flags**, such as `known` and `unknown`. Do not route on a Python boolean. See "Do not route on a boolean" in workflow-format.md.
497	- Keep snippets fast. They block the conversation.
498	- Do arithmetic, date calculation and counting in code, and give the model the finished facts as text. Verified in a working builder: it computes a block of date facts in a code node and places it in the prompts.
499	- Treat a code node like an API node: `passthrough: true`, a `passthrough_default_transition`, and a last `always` transition.
500	
501	### Sandbox limits
502	
503	| Limit | Value |
504	|---|---|
505	| Time | `timeout_ms`, default `30000` |
506	| Modules | `json`, `re` and `datetime` are verified in a working builder. The full list is not documented |
507	| Network and file access | Not documented |
508	| Memory and output size | Not documented |
509	
510	### `code_exec` as a tool
511	
512	`code_exec` can also be a tool in the `tools` array of a conversation node, called by the model. Its parameters are top-level arguments, declared without `default` so the model fills them. For such a tool the `code` field resolves `{{var}}` when the tool is called, against the current variable table. The working builder does not use this form, so nothing about it is verified here.
513	
514	## Lifecycle tools
515	
516	A tool whose `config.alwaysRunsAt` is a non-empty list is never shown to the model. The engine fires it at a fixed point of the call.
517	
518	| Value | When |
519	|---|---|
520	| `start_of_call` | During call setup, before the first turn |
521	| `end_of_call` | After the call has ended |
522	| `each_turn` | Accepted by the schema but not implemented. It never fires |
523	
524	Put a lifecycle tool that must run on every call into the workflow's top-level `tools` array.
525	
526	```json
527	{
528	  "initial_node": "greeting",
529	  "nodes": {},
530	  "tools": [
531	    {
532	      "type": "function",
533	      "config": { "alwaysRunsAt": ["end_of_call"] },
534	      "function": {
535	        "name": "push_call_result",
536	        "handler": "__function__:api_call",
537	        "parameters": {
538	          "type": "object",
539	          "properties": {
540	            "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/call-results" },
541	            "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
542	            "body": {
543	              "type": "object",
544	              "properties": {
545	                "summary": { "type": "string", "default": "{{call.analysis.summary}}" },
546	                "reason": { "type": "string", "default": "{{call.call_end_reason}}" }
547	              }
548	            }
549	          }
550	        }
551	      }
552	    }
553	  ]
554	}
555	```
556	
557	Rules:
558	
559	- A workflow-level tool without `alwaysRunsAt` never runs and the model never sees it.
560	- A lifecycle tool in a node's `tools` runs for `start_of_call` only on the `initial_node`, and for `end_of_call` only on the node in which the call ended.
561	- If a `{{var}}` parameter is still unresolved, one model call fills the parameters. If everything resolves, the handler runs directly.
562	- `response_mapping` is applied for `start_of_call`. It is not applied for `end_of_call`.
563	- At the end of a call the order is: call analysis, then `end_of_call` tools, then success-criteria judging. An `end_of_call` tool can use `{{call.analysis.summary}}`, `{{call.analysis.structured_data_str}}`, `{{call.call_end_reason}}`, `{{call.call_end_reason_category}}`, `{{call.call_tags}}` and `{{call.duration}}`.
564	- A malformed lifecycle tool is dropped at run time without an error. Validate with a dry run (api.md).
565	
566	## Tool results and the next turn
567	
568	After a tool call returns, the model sees the result and has to produce the next turn itself. Two things were seen in practice runs with the hackathon's agent model:
569	
570	- **The agent says nothing after the tool call.** The result arrives, no assistant message follows, and the simulated customer hangs up after waiting. It happens more often when the result is bare data such as `{"ok": true, "verified": true}`.
571	- **The agent ignores a negative result.** For example it reads `"verified": false` and moves on to the next question as if the answer had passed.
572	
573	What fixed both in a working builder (verified, see the post-hook section above): a post-hook on the tool that adds one plain instruction line to the result before the model sees it, for example a `what_to_do_next` field that says what the answer means and what to say or call next. The model then has something to act on.
574	
575	Also say it in the step's prompt: after every tool result, speak to the customer or call the next tool. Never end a turn with nothing.
576	
577	## Checklist
578	
579	- Fixed values use `default`, never `const`.
580	- Each `api_call` body field is a leaf under `body.properties` with its own `default`, `description` and `enum`.
581	- `tools` only on `conversation` nodes. `pre_actions` only on `api_request` and `code` nodes.
582	- `response_mapping` on the tool for `tools`, on the node for `pre_actions`.
583	- Mapping paths start with `data.`.
584	- Booleans from results are tested as `"true"` and `"True"`, or replaced by string fields.
585	- Every passthrough node ends with an `always` transition.
586	- Code reads and writes through `vars`, never raises, and contains no `{{` or `}}`.
587	- Tool descriptions say when to call the tool.
588
